title: Establishment of a telemedicine-supported prehabilitation and ERAS program in cardiac surgery - a feasibility study
summary:
Heart surgeries are a major burden for many people. Prehabilitation has proven to be safe and effective in multiple studies to reduce postoperative complications and support a faster recovery after surgery.

The aim of this feasibility study at the Robert Bosch Hospital in Stuttgart is to examine whether a special care program before and after the operation can be easily integrated into everyday hospital life. The program consists of targeted preparation before the operation (prehabilitation) in two different intensities of support and structured treatment after the operation (Fast Track / ERAS program). The preparation takes place at home and is supported with the help of digital offers (training videos, learning units, video calls).

Patients who are scheduled to undergo heart surgery are taking part in the study. Three weeks before the operation, they start home training and, if necessary, additional measures such as psychocardiological counseling or treatment of malnutrition. After the operation, they are treated in hospital according to a standardized regimen designed to promote rapid recovery.

The study examines how well the program can be implemented, how satisfied patients are with it and what form of care is sufficient. It will also record whether certain groups benefit in particular and whether complications can be reduced as a result of the measures.

interventions.name:
The intervention consists of a three-week telemedical prehabilitation program with varying levels of support and structured postoperative follow-up treatment in accordance with the ERAS principles.

Prehabilitation is carried out at home using app-supported self-training in the form of avatar-base

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Elective surgery
- Low-medium calculated surgical risk
Exclusion criteria:
- Urgent or emergency surgery
- High calculated surgical risk (EuroSCORE II > 8)
- Not able or willing to give consent
- Age < 18 years
